definition: Dancing mania is a historical term for an abnormal, excessive tendency toward rhythmic movement, especially dancing, that spread in groups under special circumstances through nervous or mental contagion. It was described as sometimes occurring in large epidemics, with choreic, spasmodic movements, dazed awareness, hallucinations, and an overpowering urge to keep dancing even to exhaustion.
